title: Presentability of an Ind completion
statement: Use the universes, $\kappa$-small simplicial sets, filteredness, compactness and accessibility of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], the coherent functors, full subcategories and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the infinity category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ of small spaces from [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal. For a small infinity category $\mathcal C$, write $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ for its space-valued presheaf infinity category, and $j(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,c)$ for Yoneda. Define $\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)$ to be the replete full subcategory of $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$ on the objects which are small $\kappa$-filtered colimits of these representables, computed in $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$. Then $j:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)$ is fully faithful, its objects $j(c)$ are $\kappa$-compact, and $\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)$ is locally small and admits small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, preserved by its inclusion into $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$. Every object is such a filtered colimit of objects $j(c)$; hence $\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)$ is $\kappa$-accessible. The functor $j$ preserves every $\kappa$-small colimit existing in $\mathcal C$. If $\mathcal C$ admits all $\kappa$-small colimits, then $\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)$ admits all small colimits and is presentable.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.1.3.1, Proposition 5.3.5.3, Corollary 5.3.5.4, Propositions 5.3.5.5 and 5.3.5.14, and Theorem 5.5.1.1(4), printed pp. 322, 403-404, 409-410, 458.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$ and $D=\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)$. The presheaf free-cocompletion statement gives local smallness of $P$ and existence of all small colimits; the pointwise-colimit statement identifies these colimits objectwise. Yoneda evaluation gives $\operatorname{Map}_P(jc,jd)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,d)$, so Yoneda is fully faithful. Each $jc$ belongs to $D$: the one-object terminal indexing quasicategory is small and $\kappa$-filtered and the identity cocone is colimiting. Fullness of $D\subseteq P$ then gives local smallness and full faithfulness into $D$. Moreover $\operatorname{Map}_P(jc,-)\simeq\operatorname{ev}_c$ preserves all small colimits by pointwise computation. It therefore preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, including as a functor into larger-universe spaces because change of universe preserves these colimits. Thus each $jc$ is $\kappa$-compact in $P$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.3.1, Lemma 5.1.5.2, Corollary 5.1.2.4; preliminary size and compactness calculation.

proof.text: For a small quasicategory $B$ and a right fibration $Z\to B$ classifying $H:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, the terminal-space constant presheaf is classified by $B\to B$. Transport classification therefore identifies the section space with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(\Delta *,H)$. The limit universal property identifies this with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(*,\lim H)$. This is $\lim H$: in the Kan model, an $n$-simplex of the mapping complex from a point is an $n$-simplex of the target; the coherent-nerve comparison identifies that mapping complex with the mapping space of $\mathcal S$. All these identifications are natural under pullback and in $H$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.3.4, opposite/sections calculation, expanded from classification and the limit universal property.

proof.text: For $X\in P$ choose a small right fibration $q_X:E_X\to\mathcal C$ classifying $X$. The mapping-space formula in transport classification identifies maps $X\to Y$ with maps $E_X\to E_Y$ over $\mathcal C$. Degreewise these maps are exactly sections of $E_X\times_{\mathcal C}E_Y\to E_X$, which classifies $Yq_X^{\mathrm{op}}$. Step 2 gives $\operatorname{Map}_P(X,Y)\simeq\lim_{e\in E_X^{\mathrm{op}}}Y(q_X(e))$. Yoneda evaluation identifies the right-fibration pullback $\mathcal C\times_P P_{/X}\to\mathcal C$ with the classifier of $X$; hence it is equivalent over $\mathcal C$ to $E_X$. Its arrows $j(q_X(e))\to X$ give the tautological cocone. Under evaluation, postcomposing this cocone with $X\to Y$ is exactly the section just described. The mapping-space colimit criterion consequently proves $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{E_X}j q_X$, with this specified cocone. This establishes canonical density, rather than taking a particular indexing category from the proof of an existence-only density node.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.3 and Corollary 5.3.5.4: canonical density derived from transport and evaluation.

proof.text: Suppose $X\in D$, with a small $\kappa$-filtered presentation by representables. Reindex it by a small $\kappa$-filtered poset using the cofinal-poset statement, applied in the cocomplete category $P$. For a $\kappa$-small diagram $K\to E_X$, its projection $q:K\to\mathcal C$ and tautological arrows give a coherent cocone $jq\to X$. The vertices of $jq$ are $\kappa$-compact in $P$ by Step 1. Apply relative cocone factorization in $P$ to this presentation, with $K'=\varnothing$: it supplies a stage $j(c)$, a cocone $jq\to j(c)$ and its full compatibility with the original cocone to $X$. For the lift through Yoneda, let $h$ be the coherent inverse on its full essential image and let $\epsilon:hj\simeq1_{\mathcal C}$ be its natural equivalence. If $\lambda:jq\to\Delta_K j(c)$ is the factorized cocone, the composite $q\xrightarrow{\epsilon_q^{-1}}hjq\xrightarrow{h\lambda}\Delta_K hj(c)\xrightarrow{\Delta_K\epsilon_c}\Delta_Kc$ is a coherent cocone in $\mathcal C$. The natural equivalences for $jh$ identify its Yoneda image with $\lambda$, including the triangle to $X$ supplied by factorization. Under the classifier identification of Step 3, these data give a cocone on the original $K\to E_X$; the join/cone comparison is taken with this boundary fixed. For $K=\varnothing$, the presentation index is nonempty, so choose a stage $j(c)\to X$; it is a vertex of $E_X$. Thus $E_X$ is $\kappa$-filtered. Conversely, if $E_X$ is $\kappa$-filtered, Step 3 is the required small filtered presentation by representables, so $X\in D$. In applying the factorization theorem its join cocone model and the coherent-transformation model are identified by the join/cone comparison; replacing an indexing category by an equivalent classifier does not change the existence of a cone. Apply the left-cone comparison in the opposite quasicategory; the opposite/cone equivalences in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] identify it with the required right cocone and preserve the fixed-boundary data.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, equivalence of (1) and (2), with filteredness proved using Corollary 5.3.4.14 and the relative lifting construction in the proof of Lemma 5.5.4.13 (printed pp. 479-480).

proof.text: Let $F:I\to D$ be a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram and form its colimit $X$ in $P$. Reindex by a small $\kappa$-filtered poset, which does not change that colimit in $P$. Given $K\to E_X$ with $K$ $\kappa$-small, use relative cocone factorization with $K'=\varnothing$ and the $\kappa$-compact vertices $jq(k)$ to factor its tautological cocone through one $F(i)$. This yields a diagram $K\to E_{F(i)}$ whose cocone to $X$ is the original one, including all coherence. Step 4 says $E_{F(i)}$ is $\kappa$-filtered, so this diagram has a cocone with representable apex; postcomposing with $F(i)\to X$ gives a cocone in $E_X$. For empty $K$, choose $i$ in the nonempty presentation index, then a vertex of the nonempty $E_{F(i)}$ supplied by Step 4. Its arrow $j(c)\to F(i)\to X$ is a vertex of $E_X$. Step 4 therefore implies $X\in D$. Finally, fullness gives $\operatorname{Map}_D(X,Z)=\operatorname{Map}_P(X,Z)$ for $Z\in D$, and $\operatorname{Map}_D(F(i),Z)=\operatorname{Map}_P(F(i),Z)$ for each $i$; the colimit universal property in $P$ restricts to $D$. This proves existence of small $\kappa$-filtered colimits in $D$ and preservation by its inclusion.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.3: closure under filtered colimits, via the canonical-elements criterion and compact relative factorization.

proof.text: For a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram $F:I\to D$, Step 5 identifies its colimit with its presheaf colimit. Yoneda evaluation now gives $\operatorname{Map}_D(jc,\operatorname{colim}_I F)\simeq(\operatorname{colim}_I F)(c)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_I F(i)(c)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_I\operatorname{Map}_D(jc,F(i))$, with the canonical cocone maps. Change of universe preserves the colimit of these small spaces. Thus $jc$ is $\kappa$-compact in $D$. Its full essential image is essentially small since $\mathcal C$ is small and Yoneda is fully faithful. By the definition of $D$, every object has a small $\kappa$-filtered representable presentation in $P$, and by Step 5 that cocone is also colimiting in $D$. These statements are precisely $\kappa$-accessibility.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.5 and Proposition 5.4.2.2; accessibility from the specified generators.

proof.text: Let $p:K\to\mathcal C$ have a colimiting cocone to $c$, with $K$ $\kappa$-small, and let $X\in D$. Write $X=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}j(c_i)$ in $P$. Each representable $j(c_i)$ takes this cocone in $\mathcal C$ to a limit diagram, by the mapping-space colimit criterion. Pointwise presheaf colimits and the limit/filtered-colimit interchange in spaces give $X(c)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_i\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(k),c_i)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(p(k))$. By Yoneda evaluation this is the actual comparison $\operatorname{Map}_D(jc,X)\to\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_D(jp(k),X)$. It is an equivalence for every $X$, so the mapping-space criterion proves that $j$ sends the given cocone to a colimiting cocone in $D$. For empty $K$, the same interchange includes the terminal limit, so existing initial objects are preserved as well.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.14, using the direct evaluation/interchange calculation instead of right-exactness terminology.

proof.text: Assume now that $\mathcal C$ admits all $\kappa$-small colimits. A pushout diagram $F:N(A)\to D$ has $A=\{0,1,2\}$ with $0<1$ and $0<2$, a finite poset. The finite-poset realization statement gives a small $\kappa$-filtered index $I$ and diagrams $G_i:N(A)\to\mathcal C$ whose Yoneda images have pointwise presheaf colimit $F$. By Step 5 they also have pointwise colimit $F$ in $D$. Choose $c_i=\operatorname{colim}_{N(A)}G_i$ in $\mathcal C$. The opposite universal-arrow theorem for the constant-diagram functor assembles these colimits and their cocones coherently into $c:I\to\mathcal C$. By Step 7, $jc_i$ is the pushout of $jG_i$ in $D$. Form $L=\operatorname{colim}_I jc_i$ in $D$, using Step 5. For every $Z\in D$, the universal properties give $\operatorname{Map}_D(L,Z)\simeq\lim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\lim_{a\in N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_D(jG_i(a),Z)\simeq\lim_{a\in N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_D(F(a),Z)$. The exchange is of two limits: a coherent cone on either iterated diagram is exactly a coherent cone on their product, so the two universal properties coincide. The equivalences respect the cocone legs. The mapping-space colimit criterion makes $L$ a pushout of $F$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, finite span application, and Theorem 5.5.1.1(4): direct construction of pushouts.

proof.text: Let $(X_s)_{s\in S}$ be a family in $D$ with $|S|<\kappa$. Reindex each chosen presentation as $X_s=\operatorname{colim}_{a\in A_s}j p_s(a)$, with $A_s$ a small nonempty $\kappa$-filtered poset. The product poset $A=\prod_{s\in S}A_s$ is small and $\kappa$-filtered: choose an upper bound separately in each coordinate for any set of fewer than $\kappa$ tuples; the empty set is included. Each projection $A\to A_s$ is cofinal. Indeed its comma poset over $b\in A_s$ is the product of $(A_s)_{b/}$ and the remaining $A_t$; choose its $s$-coordinate above $b$ and choose any point in each other nonempty factor to get an object. For any fewer than $\kappa$ such objects, choose an upper bound in each coordinate, including $b$ in the set to be bounded in the $s$-coordinate. This gives an upper bound inside the comma poset, so it is $\kappa$-filtered and the weak-contractibility clause of the coslice-colimit statement applies. Apply the cofinal-comma statement in $P$. Consequently the discrete diagrams $s\mapsto j p_s(a_s)$ have pointwise filtered colimit $s\mapsto X_s$. The $<\kappa$-fold coproducts $c_a=\coprod_{s\in S}p_s(a_s)$ exist in $\mathcal C$ and assemble coherently by universal arrows. Step 7 makes $jc_a$ their coproducts in $D$. Form $L_S=\operatorname{colim}_{a\in A}jc_a$ in $D$. For every $Z$, $\operatorname{Map}_D(L_S,Z)\simeq\lim_{a\in A^{\mathrm{op}}}\prod_{s\in S}\operatorname{Map}_D(jp_s(a_s),Z)\simeq\prod_{s\in S}\operatorname{Map}_D(X_s,Z)$. Both orders of limits represent the space of coherent cones on the diagram $(a,s)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_D(jp_s(a_s),Z)$ indexed by $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}\times S$, where $S$ is discrete. The resulting equivalence preserves the projections to each pair $(a,s)$, so it identifies the specified coproduct legs. Thus $L_S$ is a coproduct. If $S=\varnothing$, use $A=*$ and the initial object of $\mathcal C$; this also proves existence of the empty coproduct in $D$.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1(4): explicit <kappa coproduct construction by simultaneous filtered presentations.

proof.text: For an arbitrary small set $S$, let $B$ be the poset of subsets $T\subseteq S$ of cardinality less than $\kappa$. It is small and $\kappa$-filtered: regularity of $\kappa$ ensures that the union of fewer than $\kappa$ such subsets still has size less than $\kappa$ and is an upper bound, and $\varnothing\in B$. View the discrete simplicial set $S$ as the directed union of the discrete subsets $T$. Step 9 supplies colimiting cocones on every restriction of the family to $T$. The directed-union local-colimits statement assembles these apices $L_T$ coherently and identifies the space of cocones on $T\mapsto L_T$ with the space of cocones on the entire family, without assuming cocompleteness of $D$. Since $N(B)$ is small and $\kappa$-filtered, Step 5 supplies its colimit. The same assembly statement says its cocone is colimiting on the whole family. This constructs all small coproducts in $D$, including the empty one. Notice that at $\kappa=\aleph_0$ only discrete finite subsets are used, so no countability assumption on general finite-generated simplicial subsets enters.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.3.11/Theorem 5.5.1.1(4), direct directed assembly of discrete coproducts.

proof.text: Steps 8 and 10 give pushouts and all small coproducts in $D$. The small-colimit generation theorem therefore gives colimits of every small simplicial diagram. Step 6 has already proved $\kappa$-accessibility, so the definition of presentability makes $D$ presentable. This final argument uses no adjoint-functor theorem or presheaf-localization theorem, whose current DAG dependencies lead back to the present item.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1(4) conclusion, obtained here by the coproduct-and-pushout criterion.

proof_origin.place: HTT §§5.1.5 and 5.3.5, Proposition 5.3.5.15 and Theorem 5.5.1.1(4), read online, not archived in literature/. Direct compact-factorization and coproduct/pushout argument supplied to avoid a cycle through the existing localization infrastructure.
